subject: Post-call: candidate-model triage + targeted regression plan
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmesys.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@cloudwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: candidate-model triage + targeted regression plan

Tom / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. High-level recap and proposed next steps below.

Quick recap:
- Goal: narrow to 2 candidate model families for a 2-week targeted regression run vs your current hyperscaler setup. Focus on hallucination reduction, instruction-following, and latency at 256 / 1024 token windows.
- Key constraints: SSO + VPC for security review (Priya), latency SLO of 150ms P95 for small requests, and a hard cost target per 1k tokens.

Proposed immediate next steps (please confirm priorities):
1) We run a lightweight smoke suite (3–4 prompt families you sent) against Redwood candidate A/B + hyperscaler baseline (CloudWave) — deliverable: short matrix with hallucination rate, avg latency, token cost.
2) If smoke looks good, spin full regression (2 weeks) with the expanded prompt set and ACME redlines.
3) Security onboarding (Priya): share SOC2 evidence + network topology doc — see attachments.

Requested from you to prioritize by tomorrow:
- Which of the sample prompt families are highest business priority (1–3)?
- Any additional redline prompt examples we must include in the regression?

Attachments: redwood_candidate_matrix_v1.xlsx (model config matrix), sample-eval-prompts.txt, acme-map-priorities.pdf

I'll also send an internal note to align test owners and timeline.

—Olga
Olga Petrov | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmesys.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@cloudwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 17:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: candidate-model triage + targeted regression plan

Thanks Olga — good summary. Priority order for prompt families: 1) customer support extraction (high), 2) config generation (medium), 3) policy summarization (lower).

Two asks from our side: 
- Please include the hallucination detection probe we discussed (example in sample-eval-prompts.txt, section 'halluc_probe_1').
- Can you include the hyperscaler baseline results for smaller batch sizes? We see big differences there in prod.

Also, we'll need to confirm the timeline for SOC2 evidence sharing — Priya, can you take point?

Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director of Product, Acme Systems
tom.reynolds@acmesys.com | +1 (617) 555-3412
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: ACME - focused regression plan + ownership (action items)

Team — please see the external asks and proposed plan from Tom. We're targeting a rapid smoke & then 2-week regression against ACME's sample set. Action items: 

- Ben: own the smoke run (3 families) + hyperscaler baseline across two batch sizes (1, 8). Output: simple CSV with columns [prompt_family, model, hallucination_rate, avg_latency_ms, token_cost_usd]. Due EOD Thu.
- Marissa: create the regression harness for the full prompt set (include halluc_probe_1, halluc_probe_2). Add automatic regression checks for instruction-following failure modes and a hallucination flag. Set up dashboards in Console. First regression run start Mon next week.
- Olga (me): coordinate with ACME on prompt priority confirmation, schedule follow-up sync, and collect SOC2 artifacts from Priya.

Test plan notes (guidance for both runs):
- Candidate models: Redwood-A-13B (quantized int8), Redwood-B-30B (fp16 optimized) vs CloudWave-Baseline-30B (public).
- Metrics: hallucination_rate (binary mismatch vs ground truth), instruction_follow_rate (pass/fail), latency P50/P95 at token windows 256 and 1024, token_cost computed with Redwood price table (see matrix).
- Regression acceptance thresholds (preliminary): hallucination_rate < baseline + 5pp; instruction_follow_rate >= baseline - 2pp; latency P95 <= 150ms for 256 tokens (if not, fallback routing policy suggestion).

Attachments referenced: sample-eval-prompts.txt (prompt list + expected outputs).

If anything blocks you, flag in thread and we'll escalate.

—Olga
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 10:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: ACME - focused regression plan + ownership (action items)

Olga / Marissa — got it. I'll start the smoke runs this afternoon. Quick notes:
- I'll run baseline CloudWave tests with batch sizes 1 and 8 and include a single-run cold/warm KV-cache comparison.
- I'll tag outputs with run-id and push CSV artifacts to the shared Drive link you provided. Expect initial CSV + short writeup by Thu 2027-01-14 17:00 PST.

Also, for hallucination detection: I'll include token-level provenance counters where available and a quick fuzzy-match script to flag hallucinated entities vs ground truth.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-9876
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmesys.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@cloudwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: candidate-model triage + targeted regression plan — next sync

Tom / Priya — thanks for the priorities. Ben will share smoke results Thu EOD and Marissa will have the regression harness ready to kick off early next week. Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sync Monday 2027-01-18 09:00 PT to review smoke matrix and agree on regression scope.

Link to artifacts and run schedule: https://drive.redwood.com/s/DEAL-4832/eval-suite
Doc to review before sync: sample-eval-prompts.txt

If that slot doesn't work, propose alternatives and we'll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to moving to a focused run.

—Olga
